title: GPT VOICE, POCKET AI's & NOBEL PRIZE: Matt & Jimmy debate their favourite AI Stories from September & October 2024
description: Send us Fan Mail What happens when AI evolves beyond our screens and into our voices? Join us as we unravel the dynamic world of AI, starting with a humorous chronicle of our recording adventures across time zones, complete with a Scarlett Johansson voiceover mishap. From ChatGPT's new voice capabilities to CerebrusAI's cutting-edge neural processing units, we dissect the advancements setting the stage for a future where human-like interactions with technology are just a voice command away. But it’s not all smooth sailing—dive into the cost implications and legal hurdles that come with these technological leaps. Imagine a world where your digital assistant is as intuitive as a conversation with a friend. We explore the evolving landscape of AI-driven human interactions, contemplating a shift from visual interfaces to natural, language-based interactions. Discover how tools like Google's Notebook LM transform podcasting by converting text into audio, creating new avenues for audiences to engage with content. Yet, the future of podcasting isn't just about tech—it's the personalities behind the voices that captivate, from informative talks to the charm of shows like the Football Ramble. Amidst the wonders of AI, we tackle the pressing ethical and economic dilemmas it presents. Can the AI industry sustain its soaring valuations without delivering on its grand promises? Tune in as we discuss Darren Aconglu's insights into the economic impact of AI, potential market crashes reminiscent of the dot-com bubble, and the tug-of-war between open-source and corporate-controlled AI models. We even delve into the surprising recognition of AI pioneers in the realm of Nobel Prizes, questioning traditional award criteria and exploring the fine line between human creativity and machine learning. summary: A two-month news roundup covering ChatGPT's Scarlett Johansson-flavoured voice launch, Jimmy's eerie experience cloning his own voice from three 30-second clips, and PocketPal-style local open source models that now rival GPT-3.5 on a laptop. The hosts also debate an MIT economist's warning that AI can only automate 5% of jobs and could crash the market, plus Worldcoin's rebrand and the Nobel Prizes going to Hinton, Hopfield, Hassabis and Baker.
keyTalkingPoints: Advanced voice mode responds within a couple of hundred milliseconds and can be interrupted — a step change from robotic text-to-speech
Jimmy cloned his own voice from three 30-second recordings; it was convincing enough that podcast listeners might not tell the difference
Small open source models (1B-70B parameters) now run on laptops and the 70B class outperforms GPT-4 on benchmarks
Daron Acemoglu's paper argues only ~5% of tasks are currently automatable and warns of a dot-com-style crash if hype outruns returns
Nobel Prizes in Physics (Hinton, Hopfield) and Chemistry (Hassabis, Baker, Jumper) mark AI's arrival in mainstream science, though the hosts question the physics award

jimmy: Small local open source models are already good enough to replace his Claude subscription for most tasks
Devices will soon run AI seamlessly across local and cloud with users unable to tell the difference
He would not be surprised if OpenAI does not exist in five years, given it must cash the check at some point
Even strung-together AIs will lack the creative spark for new discoveries — human-AI collaboration, like protein folding, is the real pattern
matt: Voice cloning from seconds of audio means a podcast-specific AI tool is only three to six months away
We are at peak free access to frontier models — once they have your training data, commercialization will follow, strengthening the open source case
He is now completely bought into open source on political and social grounds, distrusting big tech's intentions
Acemoglu is credible and the inflated-valuation warnings from people he trusts deserve attention
